*   When the route contains no template syntax, sanitizeRoute must return the route object unchanged (equal by value).

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions (including their delimiters) from the name field, leaving surrounding text intact. For example, 'Route {{ env.SECRET }}' becomes 'Route '.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions from each entry in the paths array, keeping any surrounding text. For example, '/api/{{ env.SECRET }}/users' becomes '/api//users'.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions from each entry in the hosts array, keeping any surrounding text. For example, '{{ env.SECRET }}.test.com' becomes '.test.com'.

*   For the methods array: entries that are entirely a {{ ... }} expression (so the full string is stripped to empty) must be filtered out. If all entries are removed, the methods field must be set to null. If some entries remain non-empty after stripping, only those valid entries are kept.

*   For the headers object: any header entry whose value array becomes entirely empty after stripping must be dropped from the returned headers object. Any header entry whose key/name becomes entirely empty after stripping must also be dropped.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {% ... %} block tag syntax from string fields, in addition to {{ ... }} variable syntax.

*   sanitizeRoute must handle delimiter interleaving: a {% %} tag nested inside {{ }} syntax must be stripped, and a {{ }} tag nested inside {% %} syntax must also be stripped, preventing template injection via interleaved delimiters.

*   Unpaired delimiters (an opening {{ or {% with no corresponding closing delimiter) must be left intact and not modified.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions from the expression field, keeping surrounding text intact.

*   sanitizeRoute must handle null values for name, methods, paths, hosts, headers, and expression fields without throwing an error, returning those fields as null in the result.

Done. I implemented `sanitizeRoute` as a named export in `packages/insomnia/src/konnect/transform.ts`.

## What I added

A new "Template sanitisation" section at the end of the file with:

- **`sanitizeRoute(route: KonnectRoute): KonnectRoute`** — returns a copy of the route with all Nunjucks-style template syntax stripped from string fields.
- **`stripTemplateSyntax(input)`** — the core stripper.
- **`findNextOpening(...)`** — helper that finds the earliest `{{` or `{%`.

## Key design decisions

**The stripper is a single left-to-right scan**, not a pair of regex passes. For each opening delimiter it finds the *first matching close of the same type* (`}}` for `{{`, `%}` for `{%`) and removes the whole span. This one rule cleanly covers every requirement:

- **Interleaving/injection** — because a region ends at its own closing delimiter, any opposite-type delimiter inside it is swallowed as part of the region. So `{{ {% x %} }}` and `{% {{ x }} %}` both strip fully to `''`, with no chance for a nested tag to survive a first pass and re-form.
- **Unpaired openings** — an opening with no matching close is emitted verbatim and scanning continues past it, so `{{ x` stays `{{ x` while a valid `{% y %}` later in the same string is still stripped.
- **Surrounding text preserved** — `Route {{ env.SECRET }}` → `Route `, `/api/{{ env.SECRET }}/users` → `/api//users`, `{{ env.SECRET }}.test.com` → `.test.com`.

**Field-specific handling:**
- `name`, `paths`, `hosts`, `expression`: strip each string, keep surrounding text.
- `methods`: strip each entry, drop entries that become empty, and set the field to `null` if none remain.
- `headers`: drop any entry whose stripped key is empty or whose values all strip away.
- All of `name`/`methods`/`paths`/`hosts`/`headers`/`expression` return `null` when given `null`.

## Verification
- Existing `transform.test.ts` — 51/51 pass.
- A throwaway test covering every spec example (including interleaving, unpaired delimiters, `{% %}` blocks, null handling, and the "unchanged when no templates" case) — 5/5 pass; file removed afterward.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` on the file are clean.

I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
